sanskrit_verse:
पतितादिकृतश्चैव यश्च न प्रकृतिं गतः ।
अस्वतन्त्रकृतश्चैव पूर्वपक्षो न सिद्ध्यति ॥ १,१.१२२
transliteration: patitādikṛtaś caiva yaś ca na prakṛtiṃ gataḥ / asvatantrakṛtaś caiva pūrvapakṣo na sidhyati // BrhS_1,1.122
sph_interpretive_translation: One who acts under compulsion of fall or degradation, and one who has not attained natural state of being, and one whose actions stem from lack of sovereignty—such a one's prior claim or position does not hold validity.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority arises only from self-established consciousness, not inherited status
Causation is traced to the absence of svatantrya (self-sovereignty)
Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with prakṛti (natural order)
Restoration logic begins with reclaiming one's innate state of freedom
Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for legal standing
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, any litigant whose current condition stems from a fall from dharma or lack of svatantrya must first undergo restoration protocols before their claims are entertained. Precedents based on former positions are inadmissible until consciousness realignment is verified.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that misaligned action originates in loss of prakṛti, not willful violation. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows that disconnection from svabhāva precedes faulty conduct. Responsibility lies in completing the return to natural state, not in punitive consequence. Truth-realigning Nyaya operates through consciousness restoration, not external judgment.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate svatantrya-reclamation process for all parties demonstrating fallen condition
Assign prakṛti-alignment mentorship until self-established consciousness is regained
Suspend legal proceedings until completion of foundational integrity restoration
Implement daily śuddhi practices to remove karmic residue causing non-sovereign behavior
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of Dharma. Fallen states invalidate prior positions. Only restored consciousness holds legal ground. Reality is non-punitive. Dharma is hereby realigned.
